newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BRIGHTON SURVIVE AS HEREFORD GO OUT OF LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRIGHTON SURVIVE AS HEREFORD GO OUT OF LEAGUE.

text.p: A 1-1 draw in front of 8,532 spectators was described by two vastly experienced English soccer managers on Saturday as "the greatest day of my career" and "without doubt the worst day in my 18 years in football."
The game was between Hereford and Brighton in the third division. It was no cup final or championship decider -- it was more important than that.
An amazing quirk of the fixture computer meant that the final game of the season was between the bottom two clubs -- with league survival at stake.
Home side Hereford needed to win and deservedly led through an own goal by Brighton's Kerry Mayo.
But Brighton manager Steve Gritt sent on Robbie Reinelt as a second-half substitute and within five minutes he had scored the equaliser that ensured Brighton's survival after 77 years in the league.
Instead, Hereford, elected to the old fourth division in 1972 following their famous F.A. Cup success over Newcastle, go down to the Conference.
They will be replaced by Macclesfield, who should have come up two years ago only for the league to rule their ground unfit.

Macclesfield manager Sammy McIlroy, a former Northern Ireland international and an F.A. Cup winner with Manchester United, described the Cheshire club's achievement as his "proudest day and greatest achievement".
Gritt, who was in joint charge of Charlton when they were in the old first division from 1990 to 1992, voiced similar satisfaction.
Gritt, who took over Brighton in December when they were 11 points adrift, said his players -- and their travelling supporters -- had been "absolutely magnificent".
"The tension was unbelievable and when they went close at the end...well it would have been really cruel."
Gritt was unemployed when Brighton offered him a way back after 18 months out of game.
"I was grateful for the chance -- maybe I've shown a few people I can do the job," he said.
And he was full of sympathy for Hereford boss Graham Turner, formerly in charge of Wolves and Aston Villa.
"I would hate to be in his shoes," said Gritt. "Words cannot describe how he feels."
Turner, who said he would now resign, said it was the worst day in his 18 years in football "without a shadow of a doubt".
"We played reasonably well but it was almost destined not to go in for us," he said. "It is a terrible tragedy for the club -- we've just got to get over it.

"We've got a chance of staying full time and giving it a good go and bouncing back, but I shall offer my resignation on Monday. As manager you are responsible for things. When you get to this stage it's something you've got to do."
Both teams finished on 47 points -- 20 more than Torquay managed when finishing bottom last season -- but Hereford went down by virtue of scoring fewer goals.
